# OriginCheck

**OriginCheck** is a web app that gives an *estimate* of whether an image or a piece of text was generated by AI.

It is built around one rule: **no AI detector can identify every AI-generated image or text with certainty.** So OriginCheck never promises "full accuracy", never shows an uncalibrated model score as a probability, and answers **"Unable to assess reliably"** whenever it has no validated basis for a verdict.

> **Status:** working application and evaluation framework. **No accuracy has been measured yet** — no datasets or evaluation reports ship with this repository, so every performance metric is *Not yet measured*. The provider adapters were written from public documentation and are tested against a mocked `fetch`, **not against the live APIs**. See [Current status and caveats](#current-status-and-caveats).

## Features

- **Two flows:** *Check an image* and *Check text*, in a responsive, keyboard-accessible UI.
- **Image checks:** PNG, JPEG, WebP. Client- and server-side type and size limits. Preview with a remove button.
- **Provenance:** reads C2PA / Content Credentials through the real [`c2patool`](https://github.com/contentauth/c2patool) CLI, treated as a **separate evidence source** from the classifier.
- **Text checks:** live word/character counts, a provider-driven minimum length, and "Insufficient text to assess." below it.
- **Honest results:** every result separates the **detector score**, an **estimated probability** (only when calibrated), and the **reliability** of the result.
- **Clear states:** empty, loading, success, inconclusive, unsupported input, insufficient text, rate-limited, and service unavailable.
- **Evaluation harness:** held-out metrics with confidence intervals, calibration, per-group breakdowns, and versioned reports.
- **Privacy-first:** nothing stored, no content logged, secrets server-side only.
- **Zero npm dependencies:** built on Node's `http`, `fetch`, and `node:test`.

---

## Design principles

| Principle | How it is enforced |
|---|---|
| Never invent results | No heuristic "detectors". Only real providers; otherwise the API returns *Analysis unavailable*. |
| A score is not a probability | The raw score is always labelled as such. A probability appears only if a validated report contains a calibration fitted on separate data. |
| Verdicts need evidence | Thresholds come only from a **validated** evaluation report matching the provider name **and** model version. No report → "Unable to assess reliably". |
| Provenance ≠ proof of human origin | Missing C2PA data is never treated as "human-made". An invalid credential is never treated as AI evidence. |
| Uncertainty is visible | Reliability (low/medium/high) and its basis are always shown; low provider confidence yields "Mixed signals". |
| Don't accuse people | Text results never infer authorship, and the UI says so. |
| Privacy by default | No storage, no content in logs, temp files deleted promptly. |

## Quick start

**Requirements:** Node.js **20 or newer**. No `npm install` is needed (there are no dependencies).

```bash
# 1. Unzip and enter the project
unzip origincheck.zip && cd origincheck

# 2. Configure
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env and add your provider credentials

# 3. Run
npm run start:env          # loads .env via Node's --env-file
# open http://127.0.0.1:3000

# 4. Test
npm test
```

If you prefer exporting variables yourself, run `npm start` instead of `npm run start:env`.

### Try the UI without any credentials (demo mode)

```bash
DEMO_MODE=true npm start
```

Every result is then labelled **"DEMO — not a real analysis"**, and a banner appears on the page. The demo "detector" is a hash-based placeholder, **not** an AI detector. Demo mode is **ignored when `NODE_ENV=production`**.

### What happens with no provider configured

| Environment | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `NODE_ENV=production` (or demo off) | The UI shows "analysis unavailable" and the API returns **503 "Analysis unavailable: no detector is configured on this server."** |
| Development with `DEMO_MODE=true` | Clearly labelled demo results. |

## Configuration

All configuration is through environment variables (see `.env.example`).

### Server

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `3000` | Port to listen on. |
| `HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Interface to bind. Use `0.0.0.0` only behind a proper reverse proxy. |
| `NODE_ENV` | `development` | Set to `production` in deployment. Disables demo mode. |
| `TRUST_PROXY` | `false` | If `true`, rate limiting keys on the first `X-Forwarded-For` address. Enable **only** behind a trusted proxy that sets/overwrites that header. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `20` | Analysis requests per client per minute. |
| `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` | `8388608` (8 MB) | Maximum image size, enforced client- and server-side. |
| `MAX_TEXT_CHARS` | `50000` | Maximum text length. |
| `DEMO_MODE` | `false` | Enable labelled demo results (non-production only). |
| `ALLOW_UNVALIDATED_VERDICTS` | `false` | If `true` and no validated thresholds exist, show a text provider's *own* class label (reliability stays "low"). |

### Providers and provenance

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `SIGHTENGINE_API_USER`, `SIGHTENGINE_API_SECRET` | Credentials for image detection. |
| `SIGHTENGINE_MODEL_VERSION` | Optional. Recorded as the model version in results and used to match evaluation reports. If unset, the version is `unreported`. |
| `GPTZERO_API_KEY` | Credential for text detection. |
| `GPTZERO_MIN_CHARS` | Minimum characters accepted for text. Default `250` — **verify against GPTZero's current documentation.** |
| `C2PATOOL_PATH` | Path to the `c2patool` binary. If unset, provenance reports `not-checked`. |

Credentials are read only on the server and are never sent to the browser.

## Providers

OriginCheck uses real, documented third-party services and never fabricates endpoints, models, or results.

| Content | Provider | Docs | Data sent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Image | **Sightengine** — AI-generated image detection (`genai` model) | https://sightengine.com/docs/ai-generated-image-detection | The uploaded image |
| Text | **GPTZero** — text detection | https://gptzero.me/docs | The pasted text |
| Provenance | **c2patool** (Content Authenticity Initiative), run locally | https://github.com/contentauth/c2patool | Nothing leaves your server |

Provider privacy policies: [Sightengine](https://sightengine.com/privacy) · [GPTZero](https://gptzero.me/privacy-policy). The UI states what is sent and links the policy next to each form. Review their retention and training terms yourself before deploying.

### Important caveat about the adapters

The two adapters in `src/providers/` were written from the providers' public documentation. Their tests use a **mocked** `fetch`. They have **not** been run against the live APIs in this repository. Before relying on them, test with your own keys and confirm:

- request and response field names,
- the GPTZero minimum text length and supported languages,
- which image formats Sightengine accepts (AVIF is **disabled** in OriginCheck because support is unconfirmed — enable it by setting `supportsAvif: true` in the adapter only after verifying).

### Installing c2patool (optional but recommended)

Install `c2patool` per its repository instructions, then set `C2PATOOL_PATH=/path/to/c2patool`. OriginCheck writes the upload to a temporary file (mode `0600`) inside a fresh temp directory, runs `c2patool <file>` with a 10-second timeout, parses the JSON report, and deletes the directory in a `finally` block.

Only C2PA is inspected. There are no EXIF-based heuristics.

---

## How a result is produced

### Image pipeline

1. **Validate** the request: rate limit → size → declared `Content-Type` → magic-byte sniffing (PNG/JPEG/WebP). The declared type and the real file content must agree.
2. **Provenance check** (C2PA) — independent of the classifier.
3. **Detector call** — the image goes to the configured image provider.
4. **Validation lookup** — find the newest *validated* evaluation report matching content type, provider name, and model version.
5. **Verdict** — combine detector and provenance (rules below).
6. **Respond** — the uploaded bytes are discarded; nothing is stored.

### Text pipeline

1. Rate limit → JSON parse → type check → length checks (maximum, then provider minimum).
2. Detector call.
3. Validation lookup and verdict, as above.

### Verdict rules

**Detector verdict** (`src/verdict.js`):

- If a validated report exists, compare the raw score with its thresholds:
  - score ≥ `ai` threshold → *AI*
  - score ≤ `human` threshold → *human*
  - otherwise → *mixed*
- Else, if `ALLOW_UNVALIDATED_VERDICTS=true` **and** the provider gave its own class label → use that label (reliability stays "low").
- Else → **no verdict from the detector** (the raw score is still displayed).
- If the provider reports **low confidence** → *mixed* (inconclusive).

**Provenance:**

- A credential that is **found, validly signed, and declares AI-generated media** (IPTC digital source type `trainedAlgorithmicMedia` / `compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia`) counts as AI evidence.
- A credential that fails validation is reported but **not** used as AI evidence.
- No credential, or no `c2patool`: reported as `none-found` / `not-checked`. **Never** treated as human-made.

**Combining:**

| Provenance | Detector | Final verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Valid AI declaration | AI or none | *Signals suggest AI-generated* |
| Valid AI declaration | human | *Mixed signals* (they disagree) |
| Anything else | AI / human / mixed | that detector verdict |
| Anything else | none | *Unable to assess reliably* |

If the detector is down but a valid AI credential exists, the credential alone can produce a result (reliability *high*, with the basis stated).

### Reliability and probability

- **Reliability** (`low` / `medium` / `high`) comes from the validated report (sample sizes, false-positive CI, calibration error). With no report it is `low` with the basis "Not yet measured".
- **Estimated probability** is shown **only** if the report contains a calibration (isotonic regression fitted on a separate tuning split); otherwise it is `null` and the UI says so.

## Result format

Both analysis endpoints return the same shape (excerpt):

```json
{
  "contentType": "image",
  "verdict": "unable",
  "verdictLabel": "Unable to assess reliably",
  "demo": false,
  "detector": {
    "provider": "Sightengine AI-generated image detection",
    "version": "unreported",
    "score": 0.863,
    "scoreMeaning": "The detector’s raw model output (0 to 1; higher means more AI-like). It is not a probability that the content is AI-made."
  },
  "estimatedProbability": null,
  "probabilityNote": "Not shown: this detector has no calibration data for this content type (Not yet measured).",
  "reliability": { "level": "low", "basis": "No validated evaluation exists for this detector and version (Not yet measured)." },
  "signals": ["Detector returned a raw score, but there are no validated thresholds, so no verdict is drawn from it."],
  "provenance": { "status": "not-checked", "valid": null, "declaresAI": false, "generator": null, "note": "…" },
  "limitations": ["Cropping, screenshots, resizing, compression, and editing can change detector results.", "…"],
  "timestamp": "2026-11-02T12:35:37.000Z",
  "disclaimer": "This is an estimate, not proof of how the content was made."
}
```

`verdict` is one of `ai`, `human`, `mixed`, `unable`, with these labels:

| `verdict` | Label shown |
|---|---|
| `ai` | Signals suggest AI-generated |
| `human` | Signals suggest human-created |
| `mixed` | Mixed signals |
| `unable` | Unable to assess reliably |

Every rendered result includes: verdict, detector score with meaning, estimated probability (if any), reliability and basis, signals used (including provenance), provider and model version, key limitations, timestamp, and the note **"This is an estimate, not proof of how the content was made."**

## API reference

All responses are JSON unless noted. Security headers (CSP, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`) are set on every response.

### `GET /api/config`

Public, non-secret configuration for the UI: size limits, per-content-type availability, provider name, data-sent statement, privacy-policy URL, allowed image types, and the text minimum length.

### `POST /api/analyze/image`

- **Body:** the raw image bytes.
- **Header:** `Content-Type: image/png | image/jpeg | image/webp` (must match the file contents).

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/analyze/image \
  -H "Content-Type: image/png" --data-binary @photo.png
```

### `POST /api/analyze/text`

- **Body:** `{ "text": "…" }` as JSON.

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/analyze/text \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"<at least the provider minimum number of characters>"}'
```

### Errors

Errors use this shape and a `state` the UI maps to a screen:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "too_large", "state": "unsupported-input", "message": "…" } }
```

| HTTP | `code` | `state` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `empty_body`, `bad_request`, `bad_json` | `unsupported-input` | Missing/invalid body |
| 413 | `too_large` | `unsupported-input` | Over the size/length limit |
| 415 | `unsupported_type`, `type_mismatch` | `unsupported-input` | Wrong type, or content doesn't match the declared type |
| 422 | `insufficient_text` | `insufficient-text` | Below provider minimum ("Insufficient text to assess.") — also returns `minChars`, `chars`, `words` |
| 422 | `unsupported_by_provider` | `unsupported-input` | Provider could not process the input |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | `rate-limited` | Per-client limit hit; includes a `Retry-After` header |
| 429 | `provider_rate_limited` | `rate-limited` | Upstream provider is rate limiting |
| 503 | `analysis_unavailable` | `service-unavailable` | No detector configured |
| 503 | `provider_unavailable` | `service-unavailable` | Provider down, timed out, or credentials rejected |
| 500 | `internal` | `service-unavailable` | Unexpected error (generic message, no details) |

## User interface and accessibility

The UI is plain HTML, CSS, and ES modules in `public/` (no build step).

**Screens/states:** empty · image preview (removable) · loading (indeterminate progress with elapsed seconds) · success · inconclusive/"Mixed signals" · unsupported input · insufficient text · rate-limited · service unavailable · demo banner.

**Accessibility:**

- Skip link; semantic landmarks (`header`, `main`, `footer`).
- Tabs implemented with `role="tablist"`/`tab`/`tabpanel`, `aria-selected`, and arrow-key navigation.
- Results and errors announced via `aria-live` regions and `role="alert"`; focus moves to the result after analysis.
- Visible focus outlines, 44 px minimum touch targets, labels on all inputs.
- Responsive layout; automatic dark-mode colors via `prefers-color-scheme`.
- Result colors are never the only signal — the verdict is always spelled out in text.

**Rendering safety:** `public/render.js` escapes every provider-controlled string before inserting HTML.

## Evaluation and accuracy

Image and text detectors are evaluated **separately**. Until `eval/run.js` has actually been run on your data, every metric is **Not yet measured**.

### Workflow

1. **Collect datasets** under `eval/datasets/` (git-ignored except its README) and document each one — source, license, collection dates, size, generators, limitations.
2. **Write a manifest CSV:**

   ```
   path,label,split,source,generator,condition,language
   imgs/a1.png,ai,tune,midjourney-export,midjourney-v6,original,
   imgs/h1.jpg,human,heldout,own-photos,,jpeg-q60,
   texts/t1.txt,ai,heldout,generated-2026-10,gpt-x,paraphrased,en
   ```

   - `label`: `ai` or `human`
   - `split`: `tune` (thresholds and calibration are fitted here) or `heldout` (metrics are reported here)
   - `condition`: use it for edited / compressed / paraphrased / translated / mixed-source examples
3. **Run it** with credentials set:

   ```bash
   node --env-file=.env eval/run.js --type image --provider sightengine --manifest eval/datasets/image-manifest.csv
   node --env-file=.env eval/run.js --type text  --provider gptzero   --manifest eval/datasets/text-manifest.csv
   ```
   (or `npm run eval:image` / `npm run eval:text`). Optional flags: `--out <dir>`, `--delay-ms <n>` (pause between provider calls, default 250).
4. **Review the report** in `eval/reports/` — a `.json` file (read by the app) and a `.md` file (for humans), named `<type>-<provider>-<date>`. Commit reports to keep a versioned history and compare runs when a provider or threshold changes.

### What each report contains

- Dataset summary: counts per split and class, manifest used, failed rows.
- **Precision, recall, false-positive rate, false-negative rate, abstain rate** — each with **sample counts and Wilson 95% confidence intervals**.
- **Calibration:** isotonic mapping, plus **ECE** and **Brier score** on held-out data, and a binned reliability table.
- **Breakdowns** by `source`, `generator`, `condition`, and `language` (AI detection rate and human false-positive rate per group), so you never rely on a single aggregate number.
- Thresholds, reliability level and its basis, and a caveat.

"AI-generated" is the positive class. Abstentions (scores between the thresholds) count as misses for recall and are reported separately.

### When does a report take effect?

A report is marked `validated: true` **only** if both the tune and held-out splits each contain at least **100 AI and 100 human** samples. Otherwise the report records "Not yet measured: …" and the app ignores it. A validated report applies only when provider **name and model version** match the live result — if a provider changes its model, the app falls back to "Unable to assess reliably" until you re-evaluate. If a provider doesn't expose a version, it is stored as `unreported`; re-evaluate whenever you suspect it changed.

### Heuristics you should review

These are judgment calls, **not standards**; adjust to your risk tolerance:

- **AI threshold:** the lowest tune-set score keeping the false-positive rate ≤ 1%.
- **Human threshold:** the 5th percentile of AI scores on the tune set. Scores between the thresholds = *mixed*.
- **Reliability:** *high* if ≥ 300 per class, FPR CI upper bound ≤ 5% and ECE ≤ 0.05; *medium* if ≥ 100 per class and FPR CI upper bound ≤ 10%; otherwise *low*.

### Avoiding leakage

`tune` and `heldout` must not share items, near-duplicates, prompts, authors, or photographers. Do not choose a provider or thresholds by looking at `heldout`; if you do, collect a fresh held-out set. Where knowable, check overlap with the provider's own training data. Results describe performance on data like what you evaluated — real-world accuracy can be lower.

## Privacy and security

**Data handling**

- Submitted images and text are processed **in memory** for the request only and are **not stored**.
- The only file written is the temporary copy for `c2patool` (mode `0600`), deleted in a `finally` block.
- The server **never logs** request bodies, pasted text, images, or secrets. Unhandled errors log only the error class name.
- OriginCheck does **not** use submissions for training, and has no opt-in mechanism.
- Content goes to an external provider **only** for the requested analysis, and the UI says so beside each form.

**Application security**

- API credentials live in server environment variables only; `/api/config` exposes no secrets.
- Server-side validation of type (magic bytes), size, and structure, in addition to client-side checks.
- Request-size limits applied while streaming the body, so oversized uploads are cut off.
- Per-client sliding-window **rate limiting** (default 20/min) with `Retry-After`.
- Strict **Content-Security-Policy** (`default-src 'self'`), `nosniff`, frame denial, `no-referrer`, `no-store`.
- Static file serving is restricted to an allow-listed set of extensions within `public/`, with path-traversal protection.
- Provider errors are mapped to generic messages so keys and upstream details never reach the client.
- Request and header timeouts are set on the HTTP server.

**Your responsibilities when deploying**

- Review each provider's retention/training terms and your legal obligations (consent, children's data, GDPR-style rules).
- Don't put a logging proxy in front that records request bodies.
- Don't submit other people's content without the right to.

More detail in [`docs/PRIVACY.md`](docs/PRIVACY.md).

## Testing

```bash
npm test
```

36 tests using Node's built-in runner, covering:

- **Input validation:** accepted formats, wrong type, content/type mismatch, empty, oversize, AVIF gating, text length rules.
- **Provider errors:** rate limiting, 5xx, network failure, malformed or out-of-range responses, no secrets in error messages.
- **Verdict logic:** no validation → "Unable to assess reliably"; thresholds; low provider confidence → mixed; provenance/detector conflicts; missing or invalid credentials; calibration interpolation; demo flagging.
- **HTTP behaviour:** end-to-end through a real local server — 415/413/422/429/503 states, demo labelling, rate limiting, static-file safety, no secrets in `/api/config`.
- **Rendering:** all required result fields, the disclaimer, HTML escaping, demo banner, and each error state.
- **Evaluation math:** Wilson intervals, isotonic monotonicity, thresholds, CSV parsing.

What the tests do **not** cover: live provider APIs, a real `c2patool` binary, browser interaction, load/abuse testing.

---

## Deployment notes

- Set `NODE_ENV=production` and a real `HOST`/`PORT`; run behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy, a cloud load balancer).
- Set `TRUST_PROXY=true` **only** if that proxy sets/overwrites `X-Forwarded-For`.
- The rate limiter is **in-memory and per-process**. For multiple instances, replace it with a shared store or enforce limits at the proxy/WAF.
- Add authentication, quotas, and abuse reporting before exposing this publicly — they are not included.
- Raise the proxy's body-size limit to at least `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`.
- Run with a process manager (systemd, PM2, container restart policy).

## Extending: adding a provider

A provider is an object with this interface (see `src/providers/sightengine.js`):

```js
{
  id, name, contentType: 'image' | 'text',
  minChars,            // text providers: documented minimum length
  supportsAvif,        // image providers
  privacyUrl, dataSent,
  isConfigured(),      // true only if credentials exist
  async analyze(input) // input: { buffer, mime } or { text }
    // returns { score (0–1, higher = more AI-like), version, providerLabel, providerConfidence }
    // throws ProviderError('rate_limited' | 'unavailable' | 'unsupported' | 'bad_response')
}
```

Then: register it in `server.js`, add it to the provider map in `eval/run.js`, add mocked-`fetch` tests, and **run an evaluation** before expecting verdicts — a new provider starts with no validated report and will return "Unable to assess reliably".

---

## Known limitations

- No detector is perfect; both false positives and false negatives occur.
- **Images:** cropping, screenshots, resizing, compression, filters, and edits change results; new generators may be missed; absent C2PA data proves nothing. Only C2PA is inspected, and only when `c2patool` is installed; signer trust evaluation is whatever `c2patool` reports.
- **Text:** mixed human/AI writing, editing, translation, paraphrasing, short samples, and non-English text reduce reliability. Results must **never** be used to accuse anyone of misconduct or to infer authorship.
- The in-memory rate limiter is single-process.
- No authentication or accounts.
- Provider model versions may be `unreported`, which weakens the link between an evaluation and a live result.

See [`docs/LIMITATIONS.md`](docs/LIMITATIONS.md).

| Item | Status |

| Web app, API, validation, rate limiting, security headers | Implemented, tested locally |
| Image provider (Sightengine) | Adapter implemented; **not tested against the live API** |
| Text provider (GPTZero) | Adapter implemented; **not tested against the live API**; minimum length default needs verification |
| C2PA provenance | Implemented via `c2patool`; **not tested with a real binary**; optional |
| Evaluation harness | Implemented and unit-tested; **never run on real data** |
| Datasets / evaluation reports | **None included** |
| Accuracy, precision, recall, FPR, FNR, calibration | **Not yet measured** |
| Verdicts for real users | Appear only after a validated evaluation report exists (or `ALLOW_UNVALIDATED_VERDICTS=true`, reliability "low") |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause / fix |
|---|---|
| UI says "Analysis unavailable" | No credentials set, or you're in production without a provider. Check `.env`, use `npm run start:env`, and read the startup log lines "Image detector: … / Text detector: …". |
| Result says "Unable to assess reliably" but shows a score | Expected until a validated evaluation report exists for that provider **and model version**. |
| Result shows "Mixed signals" | Score between validated thresholds, provider reported low confidence, or provenance and detector disagree. |
| "Insufficient text to assess." | Text is below the provider minimum (`GPTZERO_MIN_CHARS`). |
| 415 on a valid-looking image | The file's real format doesn't match its declared type, or it's an unsupported format (e.g. GIF, SVG, AVIF). |
| 429 immediately | Rate limit reached; if behind a proxy, check `TRUST_PROXY` so clients aren't all sharing the proxy's IP. |
| Provenance always `not-checked` | `C2PATOOL_PATH` is unset or wrong. |
| `--env-file` error | Needs Node 20.6+ (use a current Node 20/22 LTS). |
| Validated report ignored after a provider update | The model version changed; re-run the evaluation. |
